design: RMIT (randomized multiple interleaved trials): fresh random permutation of (strategy, concurrency, workload) triples per repetition; server restarted before every run.
notes: Run on a dedicated Azure Standard_D8s_v6 VM (8 vCPU / 32GB RAM, Central India), provisioned solely for this run and deleted immediately afterward. Nothing else ran on the VM.

First attempt at this scale (before this run) silently reported 0 ops/sec for every configuration above roughly c=1000, due to the default open-file-descriptor soft limit (1024) on a fresh Ubuntu VM being far below the concurrency levels tested. Fixed in benchmarks/run_rmit_experiment.py (raise_fd_limit()) before this run; see docs/paper_draft.md section 3 for the full writeup of this pitfall.

Result: 0/144 configurations flagged bimodal, mean relative 95% CI width 0.0177 (max 0.0420), instrumentation overhead stayed under 2.31% at every concurrency level from 100 to 3000 across all three workload types (mixed/read-heavy/write-heavy), and the per-strategy cost ranking was identical across all three workloads.
